correctness.rationale: The exact posterior formula separates the first candidate from the aggregate of later listed candidates and the unseen tail. Monotone likelihood ranking bounds that aggregate below by the second-ranked likelihood and above by the list length times that likelihood; subexponential list growth preserves its exponential rate. The tail term has the fixed-list tail exponent because the remaining codebook size has rate R and the unlisted rank space has rate one when the last-rank exponent is below one. Comparing the smaller competitor exponent with the first-candidate exponent proves both strict-sign cases. The zero-gap boundary is expressly excluded.

value.rationale: Polynomial and other subexponential list sizes are a standard operating regime for list decoding. The theorem determines whether the first candidate remains asymptotically trustworthy when list size grows with block length, and establishes that the late-second-entry reliability effect survives this scaling. It is not a finite table or an arbitrary parameter slice; it supplies a reusable asymptotic boundary for a natural family of decoder outputs.
